title: Use of Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) Monies for Studies at Private Universities
what_it_is: Use of Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) Monies for Studies at Private Universities

sections.label: PSEA scheme and restricted use
sections.summary: The PSEA scheme, introduced in 2008, provided financial support for post-secondary education, with use before 2016 restricted to publicly-funded institutions and WSQ courses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The Post-Secondary Education Account (PSEA) scheme was introduced in 2008 to provide additional financial support for post-secondary education.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: Before 2016, we had restricted the use of PSEA to publicly-funded institutions, namely, Institute of Technical Education (ITE), polytechnics, autonomous universities and the arts institutions Nanyang Academy of Fine Arts (NAFA) and LaSalle, and also Workforce Skills Qualification (WSQ) courses.

sections.label: PSEA usage broadened in 2016
sections.summary: The usage of PSEA was broadened in 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Education)
sentences.text: The usage of PSEA was broadened in 2016.

sections.label: Graduate employment survey outcomes
sections.summary: The Graduate Employment Survey showed full-time permanent employment rates of graduates ranging from 17% to 60%, and median gross monthly salaries from $2,300 to $3,200.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: For example, we have the Graduate Employment Survey that is done and if you look at the full-time permanent employment rate of their graduates, it ranged from 17% to 60%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: There is also a spread in the median gross monthly salary from $2,300, to the highest of $3,200.

sections.label: EduTrust and programme quality
sections.summary: EduTrust is awarded by the Committee for Private Education based on corporate governance, administration and fee protection standards, but does not directly relate to programme content, academic quality or industry relevance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: EduTrust is something which the Committee for Private Education (CPE) awards, looking at the standards on corporate governance, administration and fee protection, but this does not directly relate to the content of the individual programmes and the quality of the academic programmes or their industry relevance.

sections.label: Course quality, relevance and PSEA appeals
sections.summary: The speaker stressed looking at course quality, relevance and outcomes, asked the Senior Minister of State to clarify he was not saying all courses by other universities lack quality or relevance, and asked if the Ministry would consider case-by-case PSEA appeals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, I will still go back to what I said earlier about the importance of looking at the quality of the course, the relevance and the outcomes in deciding where we should be encouraging people to pursue the different skills upgrading and training options.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I would like the Senior Minister of State to clarify that he is not actually saying that currently, the courses that are offered by other universities, such as reputable foreign universities that are available to students in Singapore, he is not saying that all of them lack quality or relevance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And I would like to ask whether in this sense, the Ministry would be open, at least, to looking at case-by-case appeals for the use of PSEA.

sections.label: Suitable private training provider courses
sections.summary: If suitable courses offered by private training providers can achieve those outcomes, the speaker said it is certainly something that can be looked at.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If there are suitable courses that are offered by private training providers that can achieve those outcomes, I think it is certainly something that we can take a look at.
